"'''I Want to Hold Your Hand'''" is a song by the English rock band [[the Beatles]], written by [[John Lennon]] and [[Paul McCartney]]. Recorded on 17 October 1963 and released on 29 November 1963 in the United Kingdom, it was the first Beatles record to be made using [[multitrack recording|four-track]] recording equipment.

With advance orders exceeding one million copies in the UK, "I Want to Hold Your Hand" would have gone straight to the top of the British record charts on its day of release had it not been blocked by the group's first million-seller "[[She Loves You]]", their previous UK single, which was having a resurgence of popularity following intense media coverage of the group. Taking two weeks to dislodge its predecessor, "I Want to Hold Your Hand" stayed at number one for five weeks and remained in the UK top 50 for 21 weeks in total, and was the [[List of UK singles chart Christmas number ones|Christmas number one]] of 1963.{{sfn|Gambaccini|1991|pp=27}}

It was also the group's first American number-one hit, entering the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart on 18 January 1964 at number 45 and starting the [[British Invasion]] of the American music industry. By 1 February, it topped the Hot 100 and stayed there for seven weeks before being replaced by "She Loves You". It remained on the ''Billboard'' chart for 15 weeks.{{sfn|Harry|1985|pp=66}} "I Want to Hold Your Hand" became the Beatles' [[List of best-selling singles|best-selling single worldwide]], selling more than 12 million copies.{{sfn|Harry|2000|p=561}} In 2018, ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine named it the 48th biggest hit of all time on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100.<ref name="Hot 100 turns 60">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100-60th-anniversary |title=Hot 100 turns 60 |magazine=Billboard|access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref> In the UK, it was the second-highest-selling single of the 1960s, behind "She Loves You".<ref name=bbc_10201932>{{cite web |title=Ken Dodd 'third best-selling artist of 1960s' |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/10201932 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |date=1 June 2010|access-date=7 September 2020}}</ref>

"I Want to Hold Your Hand" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles, written by John Lennon and Paul McCartney. Recorded on 17 October 1963 and released on 29 November 1963 in the United Kingdom, it was the first Beatles record to be made using four-track recording equipment.

With advance orders exceeding one million copies in the UK, "I Want to Hold Your Hand" would have gone straight to the top of the British record charts on its day of release had it not been blocked by the group's first million-seller "She Loves You", their previous UK single, which was having a resurgence of popularity following intense media coverage of the group. Taking two weeks to dislodge its predecessor, "I Want to Hold Your Hand" stayed at number one for five weeks and remained in the UK top 50 for 21 weeks in total, and was the Christmas number one of 1963.{{sfn|Gambaccini|1991|pp=27}}

It was also the group's first American number-one hit, entering the Billboard Hot 100 chart on 18 January 1964 at number 45 and starting the British Invasion of the American music industry. By 1 February, it topped the Hot 100 and stayed there for seven weeks before being replaced by "She Loves You". It remained on the Billboard chart for 15 weeks.{{sfn|Harry|1985|pp=66}} "I Want to Hold Your Hand" became the Beatles' best-selling single worldwide, selling more than 12 million copies.{{sfn|Harry|2000|p=561}} In 2018, Billboard magazine named it the 48th biggest hit of all time on the Billboard Hot 100. In the UK, it was the second-highest-selling single of the 1960s, behind "She Loves You".

The song was greeted by raving fans on both sides of the Atlantic but was dismissed by some critics as nothing more than another fad song that would not hold up to the test of time. Cynthia Lowery of the [[Associated Press]] expressed her exasperation with Beatlemania by saying of the Beatles: "Heaven knows we've heard them enough. Getting a radio weather bulletin or time signal has been impossible without running into 'I Want to Hold Your Hand'."<ref>{{cite news |title=Will We All Become Beatle Nuts? |date=10 February 1964 |newspaper=The Ottawa Journal |url=http://beatles.ncf.ca/beatlenuts.html}}</ref>  ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]''{{'}}s music critic [[David Newman (screenwriter)|David Newman]] wrote, "Terrible awful. ...It's the bunk. The Beatles are indistinguishable from a hundred other similar loud and twanging rock-and-roll groups. They aren't talented singers (as Elvis was), they aren't fun (as Elvis was), they aren't anything."<ref>Newman, David, ''Esquire'', April 1964, 'Secular Music' column, pg 58</ref> In its contemporary review of the US single, ''[[Cash Box]]'' described it as "an infectious twist-like thumper that could spread like wildfire here."<ref name=cb>{{cite magazine |title=CashBox Record Reviews |date=4 January 1964 |page=8 |access-date=12 January 2022 |url=https://worldradiohstory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/60s/1964/CB-1964-01-04.pdf |magazine=Cash Box}}{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

In his book ''[[Revolution in the Head]]'', Ian MacDonald wrote that the song "electrified American pop", adding: "Every American artist, black or white, asked about 'I Want to Hold Your Hand' has said much the same: it altered everything, ushering in a new era and changing their lives."{{sfn|MacDonald|1998|p=89}} [[Bob Dylan]] said: "They were doing things nobody was doing. Their chords were outrageous, just outrageous, and their harmonies made it all valid."{{sfn|Scaduto|1973|pp=203–04}} For a time, Dylan thought the Beatles were singing "I get high" instead of "I can't hide". He was surprised when he met them and found out that none of them actually smoked [[cannabis (drug)|marijuana]].{{sfn|Segal|2005}} [[The Beach Boys]]' [[Brian Wilson]] recalled his initial reaction to the song: "I flipped. It was like a shock went through my system{{nbsp}}... I immediately knew that everything had changed"; he said that he and [[Mike Love]] had a meeting to discuss the challenge presented by the Beatles, as "For a while there, we felt really threatened."{{sfn|Mojo Special Limited Edition|2002|p=4}} In another interview, Wilson said the song "wasn't even that great a record, but they [female Beatles fans] just screamed at it{{nbsp}}... It got us off our asses in the studio{{nbsp}}... we said 'look, don't worry about the Beatles, we'll cut our own stuff.'"<ref>{{cite AV media |people=[[David Espar|Espar, David]], [[Robert Levi|Levi, Robert]] (directors) |year=1995 |title=Rock & Roll |medium=[[Miniseries]]}}</ref>

Discussing the Beatles' musical legacy in the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Rob Sheffield]] states:
{{blockquote|The Beatles left behind more great music than anybody can process in a lifetime{{nbsp}}... Just check out "I Want to Hold Your Hand", which explodes out of the speakers with the most passionate singing, drumming, lyrics, guitars, and girl-crazy howls ever{{snd}}it's no insult to the Beatles to say they never topped this song because nobody else has either{{nbsp}}... It's the most joyous three minutes in the history of human noise.<ref>{{cite book |editor-last1=Brackett |editor-first1=Nathan |editor-last2=Hoard |editor-first2=Christian |year=2004 |title=The New Rolling Stone Album Guide |edition=4th |location=New York City |publisher=Fireside/Simon & Schuster |isbn=0-7432-0169-8 |page=[https://archive.org/details/newrollingstonea00brac/page/51 51] |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/newrollingstonea00brac/page/51}}</ref>}}

At the annual [[Ivor Novello Awards]], "I Want to Hold Your Hand" finished second in the category "The 'A' Side of the Record Issued in 1963 Which Achieved the Highest Certified British Sales", behind "She Loves You".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://theivors.com/archive/1960-1969/the-ivors-1964/ |title=The Ivors 1964 |publisher=[[Ivor Novello Awards|theivors.com]]|access-date=26 January 2019|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307003525/http://theivors.com/archive/1960-1969/the-ivors-1964/ |archive-date=7 March 2017}}</ref> The song was nominated for the 1964 [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year]]. Still, the award went to [[Astrud Gilberto]] and [[Stan Getz]] for "[[The Girl from Ipanema]]". However, in 1998, the song was inducted into the [[Grammy Hall of Fame Award|Grammy Hall of Fame]]. It has also made the list in [[The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame's 500 Songs that Shaped Rock and Roll]]. In addition, the [[Recording Industry Association of America]], the [[National Endowment for the Arts]] and [[Scholastic Press]] have named "I Want to Hold Your Hand" as one of the [[Songs of the Century]]. {{RS500S|16|it}}{{sfn|Rolling Stone|2004}} In 2010, ''Rolling Stone'' placed the song at number 2 on its list of the 100 Greatest Beatles Songs, after "[[A Day in the Life]]".{{sfn|Rolling Stone|2010}}<ref name=rollingstone_19691231>{{cite magazine |title=2: I Want to Hold Your Hand |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/lists/100-greatest-beatles-songs-20110919/i-want-to-hold-your-hand-19691231 |magazine=Rolling Stone|access-date=21 May 2013}}</ref> It was ranked number 2 in ''[[Mojo (magazine)|Mojo]]''{{'}}s list on the "100 Records That Changed the World", after [[Little Richard]]'s "[[Tutti Frutti (song)|Tutti Frutti]]".<ref>{{cite web |title=Big Bangs: 100 Records That Changed the World |date=June 2007 |work=MOJO |publisher=Rocklist.net |url=http://www.rocklistmusic.co.uk/mojo.html#100%20Records%20That%20Changed%20the%20World|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051207104904/http://www.rocklistmusic.co.uk/mojo.html#100%20Records%20That%20Changed%20the%20World|url-status=usurped|archive-date=7 December 2005}}</ref> The song was ranked number 39 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s All Time Top 100.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=The Billboard Hot 100 All-Time Top Songs (40–31) |url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-40.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080913210001/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-40.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 September 2008 |magazine=Billboard |year=2008}}</ref> In 2011, ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' included the song on its list of the All-TIME 100 Songs.<ref name=time_2793493>{{cite magazine |last=Wolk |first=Douglas |date=24 October 2011 |title=All-TIME 100 Songs: 'I Want to Hold Your Hand' |magazine=Time |url=https://entertainment.time.com/2011/10/24/the-all-time-100-songs/?hub=2793493#i-wanna-hold-your-hand-the-beatles |access-date=29 December 2011}}</ref> {{As of |2018|December}}, "I Want to Hold Your Hand" was the 18th best-selling single of all time in the UK.<ref name=officialcharts_20181214>{{cite web |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/the-best-selling-singles-of-all-time-on-the-official-uk-chart__21298/ |last=Myers |first=Justin |date=14 December 2018 |title=The best-selling singles of all time on the Official UK Chart |publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref>

Starting at the song's final week at the top of the American charts, the Beatles have the all-time record of seven number-one songs in a one-year period. In order, these were "I Want to Hold Your Hand", "She Loves You", "[[Can't Buy Me Love]]", "[[Love Me Do]]", "[[A Hard Day's Night (song)|A Hard Day's Night]]", "[[I Feel Fine]]" and "[[Eight Days a Week]]". It was also the first of seven songs written by Lennon–McCartney to top the US charts in 1964—an all-time record for writing the most songs to hit number one on the US charts in the same calendar year.

sections.heading: Cover versions and use in pop culture
sections.wikitext:
{{more citations needed|section|date=January 2017}}
Many other musicians have recorded the song. Notable examples include:
* In 1964, [[Arthur Fiedler]] & the [[Boston Pops Orchestra]] recorded an instrumental version, which rose to number 55 in the American charts.
* In 1964, Yugoslav band [[Bijele Strijele]] released a [[Serbo-Croatian]] version of the song entitled "Ljubav nas čeka" ("Love Is Waiting for Us").<ref name="janjatović30">{{cite book |last=Janjatović |first=Petar |title=EX YU ROCK enciklopedija 1960–2006 |year=2007 |publisher=self-released |location=Belgrade |page=30}}</ref>
* In 1969, soul singer [[Al Green]] covered the song.<ref name=nytimes_20131217>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/12/17/booming/the-beatles-i-want-to-hold-your-hand-then-al-greens.html |title=The Beatles' 'I Want to Hold Your Hand,' Then Al Green's |work=[[The New York Times]]|date=17 December 2013 |access-date=11 March 2014|last1=Haller |first1=Val }}</ref> 
* In 1969, the [[Moving Sidewalks]] covered the song, which appeared as a bonus track on the album [[Flash (Moving Sidewalks album)|Flash]]. The [[Melvins]] covered the song in a version based on the Moving Sidewalks' version in the 2018 album [[Pinkus Abortion Technician]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cooldadmusic.com/2019/10/matt-chrystal-interviews-king-buzzo-of.html | title=Matt Chrystal Interviews King Buzzo of the Melvins. Melvins Play the Stone Pony with Redd Kross on 10/11 | date=October 2019 }}</ref>
* In 1976, pop rock band [[Sparks (band)|Sparks]] recorded a cover version as a single, produced by [[Rupert Holmes]] and [[Jeffrey Lesser (producer)|Jeffrey Lesser]]. It was later included as a bonus track on the 1994 CD release of their 1975 album ''[[Indiscreet (Sparks album)|Indiscreet]]'' and on the 2006 "21st Century Edition" version of their 1976 album ''[[Big Beat (album)|Big Beat]]''.<ref name=discogs_388277>{{cite web |title=Sparks – I Want To Hold Your Hand |url=https://www.discogs.com/master/388277-Sparks-I-Want-To-Hold-Your-Hand |website=[[Discogs]] |date=1976 |access-date=15 November 2024}}</ref><ref name=allmusic_0028596739>{{cite web |title=I Want to Hold Your Hand – Sparks |url=https://www.allmusic.com/song/i-want-to-hold-your-hand-mt0028596739 |website=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=15 November 2024}}</ref>
* In 1980, British pop duo [[Dollar (band)|Dollar]] had a UK Top 10 hit with their cover, included on the re-release of their debut album ''[[Shooting Stars (album)|Shooting Stars]]'' (1979).
* In 1982, [[funk]] band [[Lakeside (band)|Lakeside]] covered the song as a ballad and became a Top Ten R&B hit. 
* In 1996, singer [[Manny Manuel]] covered the song in Spanish as "Dame tu mano y ven" on the compilation album ''[[Tropical Tribute to the Beatles]]''. This version peaked at number 13 on the [[Hot Latin Songs|''Billboard'' Hot Latin Songs]] chart.<ref name=allmusic_0000957349>{{cite web |url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/manny-manuel-mn0000957349/awards |title=Manny Manuel: Awards |publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=4 April 2013}}</ref> Manuel's cover led to McCartney receiving a [[Broadcast Music, Inc.|BMI]] Latin Award in 1997.<ref name=google_19970913>{{cite magazine |title=Los Premios Latino de BMI |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AQoEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA85 |magazine=Billboard |page=85 |date=13 September 1997|access-date=29 June 2015}}</ref>
* In 2007, the musical ''[[Across the Universe (film)|Across The Universe]]''{{'}}s [[T.V. Carpio|Prudence]] performed a cover version, and it was included on the soundtrack.
* In 2026, Paul McCartney performed the song for the first time in 60 years at the [[wedding of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce]].<ref name=theguardian_20260705_paul>{{cite news |last=Khomami |first=Nadia |date=5 July 2026 |title=Paul McCartney performs I Want to Hold Your Hand for first time in 60 years at Taylor Swift wedding |url=https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2026/jul/05/paul-mccartney-i-want-to-hold-your-hand-taylor-swift-wedding |publisher=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=6 July 2026}}</ref>

Many other musicians have recorded the song. Notable examples include:
* In 1964, Arthur Fiedler & the Boston Pops Orchestra recorded an instrumental version, which rose to number 55 in the American charts.
* In 1964, Yugoslav band Bijele Strijele released a Serbo-Croatian version of the song entitled "Ljubav nas čeka" ("Love Is Waiting for Us").
* In 1969, soul singer Al Green covered the song. 
* In 1969, the Moving Sidewalks covered the song, which appeared as a bonus track on the album Flash. The Melvins covered the song in a version based on the Moving Sidewalks' version in the 2018 album Pinkus Abortion Technician.
* In 1976, pop rock band Sparks recorded a cover version as a single, produced by Rupert Holmes and Jeffrey Lesser. It was later included as a bonus track on the 1994 CD release of their 1975 album Indiscreet and on the 2006 "21st Century Edition" version of their 1976 album Big Beat.
* In 1980, British pop duo Dollar had a UK Top 10 hit with their cover, included on the re-release of their debut album Shooting Stars (1979).
* In 1982, funk band Lakeside covered the song as a ballad and became a Top Ten R&B hit.

* In 2007, the musical Across The Universe{{'}}s Prudence performed a cover version, and it was included on the soundtrack.
* In 2026, Paul McCartney performed the song for the first time in 60 years at the wedding of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce.
